plan: Baseline: tests (29) and acceptance (17) all pass.
Contracts/integration applied: random ledger -> balances -> settle zeroes everyone, within len-1 transfers, input dict unchanged. Monthly periods from months_between sum to the full balances.

Edge cases applied: malformed amounts and dates (unicode digits, newline, '1.', '.5', '+1'), failed add changes nothing, participant list mutation after add, empty period, split sums over many inputs, December and year-span months.
Acceptance: the existing acceptance/ tests already cover every AC, so I did not duplicate them.
Regression, non-functional: discarded. The repo has no pre-existing logic besides the version, and there is no security or performance requirement.
Re-run command: python3 -m unittest discover -s qa (11 tests, all pass). No tests are left red on purpose.
gaps: Wrong-type inputs (a str passed as participants, a non-str amount) were not tested. Section 6 does not say what they should do.
month_end(date.max) raises OverflowError, which is not a ValueError. I did not run it (the command was blocked), so it is unconfirmed. It is far outside realistic use.
A first Bash call that combined mkdir, a heredoc and a Python snippet was blocked by the hook. I did not work around it and used the Write tool instead.

advisory.problem: AC-011 never checks that a failed add leaves earlier valid expenses untouched. The ledger is empty before every bad add, so the test only shows that nothing was recorded.
advisory.evidence: An implementation that records the payer in a seen-names set before validating the participants would be caught by the final balances() == {} check. A bug that corrupts existing state would not be caught.

advisory.problem: AC-006 only passes True as the bool. The rule is 'a bool as parts', so False is not exercised separately.
advisory.evidence: False is already rejected by the parts < 1 check, so the gap is harmless.
